subject: 🏃 Wednesday — 6 mi Easy Z2 Recovery (Wk 10 Peak)
html:
Tomorrow you have 6 miles easy — pure Z2 recovery between yesterday's track threshold and Thursday's 10-mi progression. 18 days to race day.

HR governs: target 117–144 BPM (Z2), stay under 145. Pace readout will be ~8:30–9:30 on the hilly door route — let it float freely with the terrain. If a climb pushes HR toward 145, walk the top of it. This is a flush day, not a fitness day.

Pre-run activation + posterior-chain warm-up: Hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, banded hip IR (5–10/side), then the hamstring protocol: 2×10 dynamic leg swings per side (forward/back + lateral), 10 walking hamstring reaches per side. Foam-roll posterior chain before heading out.

Hamstring check-in: Three faint right-hamstring appearances in 11 days heading into Sunday's long run. If it's quiet today, that's a green light for Thursday's progression. If it twinges during the first mile, shorten to 4 mi rather than pushing through — protecting the hamstring for the 20-miler matters more than 2 extra easy miles today.

Recovery context: Sunday's 16-miler was brutal (heat, underfueled, walk/run finish, suffer 261), and yesterday's track threshold added quality load. Your legs may feel heavy early — that's normal in peak week. Let the first mile be slow; the flush effect usually kicks in by mile 2–3.

Focus cue: Smooth, quiet feet. Shorten your stride on the descents — quick cadence, controlled landing. The patellofemoral joint prefers it, and it's a free rehearsal for SF's downhill sections.

Where you are: Week 10 of 12, Phase 3 Peak Volume — the biggest week of the build (~48 mi). Today is the easy filler; Thursday's 10-mi progression and Sunday's 20-mi dress rehearsal are the marquee sessions. Save everything for those. Morning slot — get it done early, hydrate well through the workday, bed by 10.
